outOfScope: Global scheduler, role registry or organization workflow graph.
Exactly-once event transport or transactional outbox as a correctness prerequisite.
Deployment, AcceptanceSnapshot or Product QA semantics.
Execution-policy or strategy selection inside the activation boundary.
constraints: Event or queue delivery is not lifecycle, claim or execution authority.
Activation is not strategy selection and is not obligation creation.
Queue, cursor and local backoff state are disposable and reconstructable from canonical work state.
A stale queued hint cannot resurrect invalidated work.
Frontend and Backend independence is governed by exact semantic dependencies, not global development stages.
A durable runtime such as Restate may host activation mechanics but cannot become organizational source of truth or hidden scheduler.
invariants: one domain outage must not block unrelated domain work
queued stale hints cannot resurrect invalidated work
architectureDecisions: DOMAIN_ACTIVATION is a domain-local level-triggered reconciler over canonical actionable work. Events/polls/restart scans are wake-up hints only; every reconcile re-reads current OrganizationWork, owningDomain and obligation/currentness before claim.

Activation keys are exact {projectId,workId,owningDomain}. Activation never ranks work, selects role/stage, creates obligations, resolves ExecutionPolicy/ExecutionStrategy, or accepts principal/strategy/runtime authority from a trigger.

Canonical owning-domain scans are the recovery source. Duplicate hints converge through existing organization claim/release fencing plus ExecutionAttempt currentness; missed/lost hint state cannot strand canonical work.

BB-052 is a hard WORKER dependency. Its delivered contract must preserve CrossDomainObligation.requiredArtifactRefs into OrganizationWorkContract.requiredArtifactRefs and expose exact obligation currentness; otherwise BB-053 returns to RESEARCH_SA.

DomainExecutionInput is a new immutable content-addressed artifact referenced by OrganizationWorkContract.requiredArtifactRefs. It carries execution data missing from the generic work envelope: owningDomain, workloadType, repository ref/revision, requiredFiles and constraints. It is product input data, not activation or execution authority.

DomainExecutionController is extended generically so runtimeAdapter.dispatch/recover receives the exact immutable OrganizationWorkContract in addition to ExecutionAttemptBinding. The controller still resolves policy/strategy itself; activation passes no domain-specific execution payload.

Each workload requires exactly one domain-execution-input:sha256:* ref in requiredArtifactRefs. Runtime adapters resolve it, verify input owningDomain/workloadType against the WorkContract, and fail closed on zero/multiple/mismatched inputs.

BackendExecutionStrategy maps {WorkContract,DomainExecutionInput} deterministically to existing BackendObjective: id=boardItemId, task=summary, repository=input.repository, requiredFiles=input.requiredFiles, constraints=input.constraints; then uses existing prepare/run/recover Backend application primitives and stops before QA cross-domain control.

Frontend is a first-class independent domain with FrontendObjective/WorkOrder/Context/WorkResult/Completion contracts structurally parallel to Backend and its own runtime adapter. It consumes only its WorkContract + DomainExecutionInput and never reads Backend stage/session/completion state.

BACKEND and FRONTEND are composed as separate domain runtimes with separate trusted principals, activation controllers, DomainExecutionController instances and runtime adapters. Shared immutable/CAS stores arbitrate currentness only; there is no cross-domain stage lock or next-role dispatcher.

Parallel acceptance requires both unrelated FE/BE reconciles to reach runtime dispatch before either may complete, with distinct workContractRef, executionPolicyRef, executionStrategyRef, executionAttemptId and runtimeInvocationKey. One adapter failure must not block the other domain.
implementationSlices: D1 — DomainExecutionInput bridge [AC-5, AC-6]: add domain-execution-input.js with immutable schema {kind:'DOMAIN_EXECUTION_INPUT',version:1,owningDomain,workloadType,repository:{ref,revision},requiredFiles[],constraints[]} and content-addressed ref domain-execution-input:sha256:<digest>. A WorkContract is executable only when requiredArtifactRefs contains exactly one such ref whose domain/workload matches the contract. Add registry put/resolve over the existing immutable artifact store.

D2 — Generic execution adapter seam [AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, INV-4, INV-5]: extend DomainExecutionController runtimeAdapter calls from {binding,input,runtimeInvocationKey} to {binding,contract,input,runtimeInvocationKey}; contract is the exact immutable OrganizationWorkContract already resolved from the released claim. Existing policy/strategy resolution and attempt binding stay authoritative. Activation never supplies strategy/runtime/domain input.

D3 — Activation [AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, AC-8]: domain-activation-source.scan({owningDomain}) wraps createOrganizationWorkDiscovery.listEligible. domain-activation.reconcile({projectId,workId,owningDomain}) re-reads the exact eligible subject, binds the controller's configured principal/domain, uses existing claim/release, rechecks BB-052 currentness immediately before execution, fences drift, then calls the prebuilt DomainExecutionController with only {itemId,claimGeneration,receiptRef}.

D4 — Backend adapter [AC-5, AC-6]: backend-execution-strategy resolves the single DomainExecutionInput from contract.requiredArtifactRefs, validates BACKEND/workload match, builds BackendObjective {id:contract.boardItemId,task:contract.summary,repository:input.repository,requiredFiles:input.requiredFiles,constraints:input.constraints}, then delegates to existing prepare/run/recover Backend application primitives. It emits DomainExecutionController runtime-result shape and never invokes runBackendThenQaObjective.

D5 — Frontend domain [AC-5, AC-6, INV-6, INV-7]: frontend-contracts defines FrontendObjective/WorkOrder/Context/WorkResult/Completion with the same id/task/repository/requiredFiles/constraints input shape and FE-specific evidence claims; frontend-worker/application provide execute/recover; frontend-execution-strategy performs the same deterministic WorkContract+DomainExecutionInput mapping for FRONTEND only.

D6 — Independent runtime composition [AC-5, AC-6, AC-7]: domain-runtime-composition constructs two independent runtime objects: {owningDomain:'BACKEND',principal,activation,executionController,backendAdapter} and {owningDomain:'FRONTEND',principal,activation,executionController,frontendAdapter}. There is no switch on owningDomain that chooses a strategy and no Backend-first/Frontend-first control edge.

D7 — Proofs [AC-1..AC-8]: fe-be-parallel.test creates unrelated BACKEND/FRONTEND WorkContracts, DomainExecutionInputs, ACTIVE policies and distinct strategy descriptors; Promise.all starts both reconciles, each adapter raises dispatchStarted then waits on its own barrier; assert both dispatchStarted and distinct contract/policy/strategy/attempt/invocation identities before either barrier is released. Reject one adapter and prove the other completes. activation-recovery and partial-invalidation prove lost-hint rediscovery, duplicate convergence and stale-hint fencing.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Persisted actionable work is rediscovered and processed after controller restart even when its original notification was lost.
evidenceRequired: Fresh host with no hint/timer state immediately scans listEligible(domain) and enters claim/execution without an event.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Concurrent duplicate hints for one work item converge to one current claim/execution path.
evidenceRequired: Concurrent notify+scan for one exact key converge to one current claim/attempt; duplicate becomes NOOP/replay.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A wrong-domain activation attempt cannot claim or execute the work.
evidenceRequired: Wrong-domain principal/controller is rejected before executable claim or execution entry.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Obligation supersession between activation pre-check and execution entry prevents execution through the post-release currentness recheck.
evidenceRequired: Supersede the exact obligation after pre-check; post-release recheck fences claim and prevents dispatch.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Frontend and Backend work can progress concurrently and independently under their own domain execution strategies.
evidenceRequired: Fixture has two unrelated WorkContracts and two content-addressed DomainExecutionInputs, one BACKEND and one FRONTEND, each matched to a distinct ACTIVE execution policy/strategy descriptor.

Promise.all starts both domain reconciles; both adapters must emit dispatchStarted and distinct workContractRef/executionPolicyRef/executionStrategyRef/executionAttemptId/runtimeInvocationKey before either barrier is released.
Each adapter maps only its own exact WorkContract + DomainExecutionInput; activation contains no strategy switch or domain application mapping.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An outage in one domain leaves unrelated work in another domain actionable and able to progress.
evidenceRequired: Reject/fail one domain runtime adapter after both domains are independently admitted; the unrelated domain still reaches its own current terminal/completion state.
No shared stage flag, adapter lock or other-domain completion state participates in discovery, claim, attempt creation or dispatch.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Removing a manual next-role dispatcher does not stop progress for persisted actionable work.
evidenceRequired: No nextRole/nextDomain/stage API exists; with no event, startup/periodic domain scans still discover and reconcile persisted work.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Partial upstream invalidation suppresses only affected activation subjects while unrelated domain work remains actionable.
evidenceRequired: Invalidate one exact subject; only it becomes NOOP/fenced while unrelated domain work executes.
Deleting hint state changes no canonical truth; restart scan rediscovers work.
Activation accepts exact work keys and exposes no ranking/next-work API.
Activation cannot supply strategy; DomainExecutionController policy remains required.
Frontend is blocked only by explicit semantic dependencies, not Backend stage state.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: one domain outage must not block unrelated domain work
evidenceRequired: One-domain failure leaves unrelated domain progress running.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: queued stale hints cannot resurrect invalidated work
evidenceRequired: Stale hint after invalidation cannot claim/execute.

invariantCoverage.invariant: one domain outage must not block unrelated domain work
queued stale hints cannot resurrect invalidated work

negativeVerificationCases: Trigger/event fields cannot authorize principal, claim, execution, strategy, runtime or publication.
Role/stage activation without exact {projectId,workId,owningDomain} is rejected.
Wrong-domain controller/principal cannot claim or execute work.
Lost queue/cursor/hint state cannot strand canonical actionable work.
Duplicate scan+event hints cannot create two current claim generations or execution attempts.
Activation cannot choose ExecutionPolicy/ExecutionStrategy or create CrossDomainObligation.
Zero/multiple/mismatched DomainExecutionInput refs fail before domain application execution.
A FE/BE test is not parallel unless both dispatchStarted observations exist before either completion barrier is released.
Frontend cannot read Backend stage/session/completion as an implicit barrier.
A stale queued hint after selective invalidation cannot resurrect executable capability.

laneContracts.input: BB-053 OBJECTIVE + current BB-048 Living truth + BB-052 dependency contract
exact READY plan + DONE BB-052 consolidated truth
laneContracts.binding: plan hash + candidate SHA/tree + criterion evidence + Jev judgment
laneContracts.convergence: all criteria and Living Docs SATISFIED on exact candidate

verificationScopeNote: BB-053 uses criterion-specific activation/recovery/parallelism/invalidation checks plus existing organization/domain-execution regressions and the full agentic regression suite. Workspace-wide npm run verify remains repository CI, not semantic evidence for an individual Integration D criterion.

livingDocs.statement: The delivered Integration D Living Docs accurately describe domain-local level-triggered activation, claim/execution admission, FE/BE independent domain strategies, recovery and non-authoritative wake-up hints.

autonomyContract.host: One DomainActivationHost per owningDomain. start() immediately calls createOrganizationWorkDiscovery(...).listEligible({owningDomain}); scanOnce() derives exact {projectId,workId,owningDomain} keys and Promise.allSettled(reconcile(key)) for every eligible subject, then arms that host's next scan. notify(key) is latency-only. Scan order has no priority/authority meaning.
autonomyContract.isolation: BACKEND and FRONTEND hosts have separate principal/controller/execution-controller/runtimeAdapter and loop/timer/error state. Composition starts both without awaiting either. A rejected scan/reconcile/dispatch is local to that host and cannot cancel or gate its sibling.
autonomyContract.admission: reconcile re-reads exact work and domain; claim/release uses the host's trusted principal; exact BB-052 currentness is rechecked after release; drift fences the claim. Activation calls execution with {itemId,claimGeneration,receiptRef} only; owningDomain+workloadType policy remains sole strategy authority.
autonomyContract.backend: BACKEND runtimeAdapter wraps existing Backend prepare/run/recover only; serial Backend→QA composition is not reused.
autonomyContract.frontend: FrontendWorkOrder derives {workContractRef,projectId,itemId,summary,requiredArtifactRefs,expectedArtifactKind,expectedOutputRefs,acceptanceRefs} from OrganizationWorkContract. FrontendContext resolves only requiredArtifactRefs. FrontendWorkResult maps APPLIED|BLOCKED|FAILED plus outputs/evidence to runtimeAdapter result. Completion evaluates acceptanceRefs/evidence; recovery reuses the same attempt binding. No Backend stage/session/completion input exists.
autonomyContract.proof: Persist unrelated BACKEND+FRONTEND work with distinct active policy/strategy descriptors; start both hosts; each adapter emits dispatchStarted and waits on its own barrier. Before either release, assert both started and distinct workContractRef/policyRef/strategyRef/attemptId/runtimeInvocationKey. Fail one adapter and require the other to complete independently.
autonomyContract.noDispatcher: No nextRole/nextDomain/stage-transition API. Persisted work progresses from each domain host's startup/periodic canonical scan even with no notify/event; restart needs no queue/cursor.

domainExecutionInputContract.producerBoundary: The upstream accepted domain publication creates this immutable data artifact and places its ref in CrossDomainObligation.requiredArtifactRefs; BB-052 materialization preserves the ref unchanged in OrganizationWorkContract.requiredArtifactRefs.
domainExecutionInputContract.consumerBoundary: DomainExecutionController passes exact WorkContract to the selected runtime adapter. The adapter resolves exactly one matching DomainExecutionInput and maps it to its domain application contract.
